thesis: The coherent short thesis is that AI demand is real but the market overestimates the economics: Microsoft is shifting from software-like capital intensity toward an accelerator/datacenter cycle with lower gross margins, rapid hardware refresh and heavy upfront commitments. A large drawdown is plausible if owner FCF/share fails to recover while real yields remain high. However, current evidence does not establish accounting impairment, financing dependence, moat collapse, subsidy-driven demand, fatal concentration or structural incremental-ROIC destruction.

evidence.claim: FY2026 OCF was $182.935B but PP&E additions were $115.948B, leaving simple OCF-minus-capex of roughly $66.987B and about $9.02/share.
Microsoft Cloud gross margin was 66% for FY2026 and 65% in Q4, with AI infrastructure and usage explicitly cited as pressure points.
evidence.source: Microsoft FY26 Q4 Investor Metrics and earnings call

evidence.claim: Q4 capex was about $41B and management said roughly two thirds was for short-lived assets, mainly CPUs and GPUs, underscoring refresh-cycle and depreciation risk.
Commercial RPO reached $678B; all sequential RPO growth came from customers outside frontier model companies, and RPO excluding OpenAI grew 25%.
Management concluded ICFR was effective and the independent auditor issued unqualified opinions on both financial statements and internal controls.
The frozen DCF values Bear/Base/Bull at roughly $134.9/$441.3/$712.5 against a $497.75 price, so current valuation requires strong FCF recovery but not a Bull-plus scenario.

counterevidence: Azure grew rapidly and management said newly delivered capacity was quickly monetized, arguing against a current demand shortfall.
The balance sheet remains net cash and FY2026 OCF is enormous, limiting the probability that capex intensity becomes a financing crisis.
Microsoft’s moat spans identity, productivity, security, developers and cloud infrastructure rather than depending on one AI model.
RPO excluding OpenAI grew materially, weakening the thesis that current cloud growth is a single-customer artifact.
unknowns: Full-cycle incremental ROIC after accelerator depreciation and replacement capex.
Steady-state gross margin and owner FCF/share for AI workloads.
Economic dependence on OpenAI/frontier-model partnerships after current contracts mature.
Regulatory impact on Microsoft’s ability to bundle and distribute AI across the enterprise stack.
falsifiers: Owner FCF/share rises materially over FY2027-29 while Cloud gross margin stabilizes despite continued AI growth.
Azure/AI gross profit compounds faster than sustaining capex and depreciation over multiple years.
Copilot/agent adoption produces measurable retention, ARPU and workload expansion without rising net dilution.

hard_veto_flags.veto: 경영진 정직성 또는 회계 신뢰성 훼손
hard_veto_flags.rationale: FY2026 ICFR was effective and the independent auditor issued unqualified opinions. Investment gains make GAAP net income noisier, but the effects are transparently reconciled rather than concealed.
Microsoft has net cash and $182.9B of FY2026 operating cash flow; the AI buildout is internally funded and does not require structural equity issuance.
Paid M365 seats, Azure consumption, broad commercial bookings and ex-OpenAI RPO growth provide direct evidence of willingness to pay without material subsidy dependence.

Capital intensity and full-cycle returns are unresolved, but rapid monetization of added capacity, strong Azure growth and broad RPO do not establish a structural ROIC collapse. This remains the principal monitoring risk, not a confirmed veto.
Model commoditization is a real threat, but current evidence shows expanding usage and monetization across Azure, M365, GitHub and security rather than persistent ecosystem contraction.

hard_veto_flags.veto: 단일 제품·단일 고객·단일 규제에 대한 치명적 종속성
hard_veto_flags.rationale: OpenAI concentration is material but not fatal: sequential RPO growth came from customers outside frontier model companies and ex-OpenAI RPO grew 25%; Microsoft also has multiple independent profit pools.

key_kpis.name: Incremental AI gross profit / sustaining capex
key_kpis.threshold: Gross-profit growth should increasingly exceed depreciation and replacement-capex growth

key_kpis.name: Cloud gross margin and owner FCF/share
key_kpis.threshold: Cloud GM stabilizes/rebounds and owner FCF/share rises from the FY2026 capex-depressed anchor

key_kpis.name: RPO ex-OpenAI / customer concentration
key_kpis.threshold: Broad-customer backlog and revenue grow faster than frontier-model concentration

next_checks: FY2027 Q1 capex, depreciation, OCF and Agents and Infra margins.
OpenAI/frontier-model share of RPO and Azure growth.
Any regulatory remedy affecting M365/Azure/AI bundling or distribution.
